title: ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps
summary: ArchiveLens replaces manual or purely geometric historical map digitization workflows with a three-stage pipeline that extracts building footprints via YOLOv11-seg, classifies materials via deterministic HSV color thresholds, and parses attributes via a quantized vision-language model, then integrates results into a hybrid spatial-temporal RAG architecture with provenance grounding. The system requires georeferenced historical map sheets (a specialized dataset), a YOLOv11-seg segmentation model, a quantized VLM, and a custom ST-RAG infrastructure combining dense retrieval with symbolic spatio-temporal filtering, representing a moderate engineering investment. Failure modes include domain shift when applied to non-Sanborn map styles or different historical periods, potential hallucination or misattribution from the VLM despite prompt constraints, accumulated errors across the decoupled stages (segmentation errors propagating to classification), and the scalability of the hybrid retrieval system to larger corpora.
rationale: This is a highly domain-specific application targeting historical map digitization rather than a general-purpose technique; unless the reader works in digital humanities or cultural heritage GIS, this falls outside typical production ML engineering concerns and warrants observation rather than adoption.
